Preserve guidelines
Public access to certain areas of the Preserve is limited.
One sealed electric motor per boat may be used after first
obtaining a Boat Permit from the City's Utility Systems
Department (PSLUSD). Permit applications are available
at PSLUSD or can be obtained by calling 772-873-6400
Catch and release fishing is allowed. A Florida freshwater
fishing license may be required for those 16 years of age
or older. Wading is not permitted.
Kayaks and canoes are allowed in designated areas only.
Please note that personal flotation devices are required
for each person occupying a canoe or kayak. A lifeguard is
NOT on duty.
Per Florida statute, helmets are required for equestrians
and cyclists under the age of 16. For safety reasons, we
recommend riders of all ages wear appropriate safety
gear.
Beware of natural, uneven terrain. Drive, park, walk,
bicycle, and horseback ride at your own risk.
Beware of alligators, snakes, bobcats, panthers, feral hogs,
and other natural wildlife.
Domestic pets must be kept on a leash no longer than six
feet, and dogs must have a current rabies vaccination.
Legitimate service animals are permitted.
The following activities are prohibited:
• Collection, destruction, or disturbance of plants,
animals, rocks, minerals or other natural resources
on Preserve property
• Littering/dumping
• Fires, all types including, charcoal barbecues,
bonfires, etc. without a camping reservation
• Fireworks
• Hunting and archery
• Swimming or wading
• Alcoholic beverages without camping reservation
• ATVs, dirt bikes, or other off-road/recreational
vehicles
• Gas-powered motorized watercraft and
remote-controlled boats and planes
